It is the case of the plaintiff that the defendant had approached to the plaintiff and requested for a friendly loan of Rs.

As per the version of the defendant as well as DW-1 (Nitin Kumar) who is the husband of the defendant, the plaintiff had attended the 'kuan poojan'
ceremony of his son celebrated on 22.12.2018 and after receiving the gifts and cash collected, they returned the amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- to the plaintiff then and there in the morning of 23.12.2018 and after few days the plaintiff deposited the said amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- in his account.

Though the plaintiff has submitted in his cross examination that the said amount was paid to him by his brother Rajesh as his share of the crop production of the land but in corroboration of the same neither the said Rajesh Kumar has been examined before this Court nor it seems probable that the said Rajesh Kumar had given the exact amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- to the plaintiff as his share of land.
As per the statement of the plaintiff made during cross examination the land is about 27 bigha and the rate of contract is about Rs. 6,000/- per bigha and he is having 1/4th share in the said land.

Thus, if the rate of contract is multiplied CS No. 102/2021 Surender Prasad Vs. 23.

In his cross examination PW-1 had specifically stated that he had not sent any legal notice to the defendant Poonam between the period December 2018 till December 2020 demanding the amount of Rs. 1,50,000/-.

Further, the circumstances of the case revealed that the plaintiff had issued the legal notice dated 21.12.2020 to the defendant only after filing of FIR against the plaintiff and his family members on 26.07.2020 bearing No. 0054/2020 U/Sec.498-A/323/504/307 IPC and before that no demand has been shown to have been made by the plaintiff from the defendant regarding the said amount.

Punam Tanwar Page No. 22 of 25 the plaintiff and due to cruel treatment meted out to the sister of the defendant, an FIR was lodged against the plaintiff and other family members and thereafter the legal notice dated 21.12.2020 was issued on behalf of the plaintiff to the defendant thereby demanding the sum of Rs. 1,50,000/- from the defendant.

The circumstances further supports the version of the defendant that the said amount was returned to the plaintiff within a short period of time after kuan poojan ceremony in the morning of 23.12.2018 by the defendant and her husband and since at that time the relations between the parties were cordial and the plaintiff had also attended the kuan poojan ceremony as revealed from the photograph Ex. DW-1/1 filed on court record, the parties might not have insisted upon execution of receipt for payment of the said amount.

Further, the plaintiff has not explained to the satisfaction of this Court about depositing the amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- in cash in his account on 24.12.2018 immediately after the kuna poojan ceremony and further the explanation given by the plaintiff that the said amount was given as his share in the crop production of land by his brother Rajesh Kumar does not seem to be proper as the share of the plaintiff as per the rate and area given by the plaintiff comes only to Rs. 40,500/- and not Rs. 1,50,000/-.

Thus, there is a high probability in the present case that the defendant had given the amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- to the plaintiff soon after the kuan poojan ceremony as around 550 persons had attended the said function and substantial cash was received in the said function as gifts to the mother and the child.

Further, the later events show that the demand was made by the plaintiff only after lodging of FIR by the sister of defendant namely Neelu on 26.07.2020 U/Sec. 498-A/323/504/307 IPC and the present case seems to have been filed by the plaintiff CS No. 102/2021 Surender Prasad Vs. Punam Tanwar Page No. 23 of 25 against the defendant as a counter blast to the said FIR.

24. Further, the testimony of DW-1 namely Nitin Kumar, who is the husband of the defendant seems to be clear, trustworthy and reliable and inspires the confidence of this Court and the version of the defendant as well as DW-1 seems to be correct and probable and no such fact has come on record during the cross examination of the defendant witness which may cast a reasonable doubt on his testimony.
Further, the testimony of DW-1 seems to be corroborated by the dates and events as well as documents filed on record.

12 25.

Thus, it seems that the amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- was given by the defendant to the plaintiff soon after the kuan poojan ceremony on 23.12.2018 and for this reason, the said amount reflects in the statement of account of the plaintiff as cash deposit on 24.12.2018.

Hence, due to these reasons this Court find no merit in the case of the plaintiff that the defendant despite repeated requests and demands as well as issuance of legal notice dated 21.12.2020 failed to pay the said loan amount to the plaintiff.
The circumstances of the case, the conduct of the parties and the documents filed on record show otherwise.

Thus, on these reasons this Court deems fit to dismiss the suit filed by the plaintiff as the plaintiff has failed to discharge the initial burden to prove his case before the Court and the case of the defendant as stated in the W.S., testimony of DW-1 as well as documents filed on record cast a reasonable doubt on the case of the plaintiff.
Further, the judgment filed by the counsel for the plaintiff seems to be not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
